title: A Standardized Unpredictable Chronic Stress Protocol for Adult Zebrafish
author: Gallas‐Lopes, Herrmann, et al.
materials: Following the publication of this pioneering study, our group has successfully applied the UCS protocol across several experimental contexts. Researchers within our laboratory later replicated the earlier results showing that UCS induces behavioral and neuroendocrine alterations in zebrafish. They further demonstrated that anxiolytic and antidepressant drugs can prevent these effects, adding predictive validity to the model (Marcon et al., 2016). This suggests that the UCS protocol could potentially be used as a screening tool for evaluating new drugs aimed at treating psychiatric disorders with stress‐related origins. In subsequent studies, the protocol was also applied to investigate non‐pharmacological interventions such as environmental enrichment (EE) (Marcon, Mocelin, Benvenutti, et al., 2018; Marcon, Mocelin, Sachett, et al., 2018). EE mitigated the effects induced by UCS on behavior and cortisol levels and prevented the impacts on oxidative stress parameters and pro‐inflammatory markers. Furthermore, the UCS protocol has been employed to test various molecules with antioxidant, anti‐inflammatory, neuroprotective, anxiolytic, and antidepressant properties (Bertelli et al., 2021; Marcon et al., 2019; Mocelin et al., 2019; Sachett et al., 2022).

Beyond pharmacological testing, the UCS protocol has facilitated studies on the neurobiology of stress, examining behavioral, physiological, and molecular outcomes (Chakravarty et al., 2013; Demin et al., 2020; Fulcher et al., 2017; Grzelak et al., 2017; Manuel et al., 2014; Pavlidis et al., 2015; B. R. Reddy et al., 2021). Furthermore, the protocol has been used to evaluate non‐pharmacological interventions such as EE (Marcon, Mocelin, Benvenutti, et al., 2018; Marcon, Mocelin, Sachett, et al., 2018). This adaptability makes the UCS protocol a tool for studying stress‐related conditions like anxiety, depression, post‐traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and increased susceptibility to substance abuse, providing insights into potential therapeutic strategies (Al‐Zoubi et al., 2024; Gallas‐Lopes, Bastos, et al., 2023; Nguyen et al., 2014).

steps.title: Prepare housing and assign groups
steps.instruction: Allocate adult zebrafish to experimental groups, keep tanks in the same room, and randomly distribute the tanks within the housing system to avoid environmental bias.

steps.title: Configure tank environment
steps.instruction: Install visual barriers on the sides of each tank while leaving the front unobstructed, code tanks to mask group identity, place a net inside each tank for the entire experiment, and use static tanks with individual filtration (no recirculating water) to prevent spread of alarm substances.

steps.title: Start UCS regimen
steps.instruction: Begin the unpredictable chronic stress (UCS) protocol on the day after group allocation; maintain standard husbandry, consistent feeding routines, and minimize tank cleaning or other disturbances throughout the protocol.

steps.title: Apply stressors twice daily for 14 days
steps.instruction: For 14 consecutive days, expose each fish to one stressor twice per day (approximately 12‑hour interval) in a randomized order and at variable times to prevent habituation.

substeps.instruction: Select a stressor at random from the following list for each exposure:
• Social isolation (place fish alone in a separate tank).
• Overcrowding: place 10 fish together in a beaker.
• Lowering water level in the tank.
• Tank change (transfer fish to a clean tank).

Apply the chosen stressor according to its standard implementation (e.g., temperature change, crowding, predator introduction) and then return the fish to its home tank before the next scheduled exposure.

steps.title: Maintain consistent husbandry during protocol
steps.instruction: Keep feeding schedules identical across all groups, avoid any additional handling beyond the scheduled stressors, and continue to minimize any non‑protocol disturbances (e.g., tank cleaning) for the entire 14‑day period.
